name: Nodular Cutaneous Amyloidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Nodular Cutaneous Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits in skin biopsy with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Presence of waxy, firm, yellowish to reddish nodules or plaques localized to the skin without systemic involvement
Immunohistochemical identification of AL (light chain) amyloid subtype in skin lesions
Exclusion of systemic amyloidosis by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits in skin biopsy plus clinical presence of characteristic nodules or plaques
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Systemic amyloidosis must be excluded to confirm localized nodular cutaneous amyloidosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Waxy, firm, yellowish to reddish cutaneous nodules or plaques
searchTerms: hard skin plaques with waxy texture

pathognomonic.symptomName: Amyloid deposits confirmed by Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence
searchTerms: tissue with apple-green birefringence under microscope
local pain or discomfort at nodules
small swollen lymph nodes in area
disease spreading to whole body amyloid

rare.symptomName: Local nerve involvement causing sensory changes
searchTerms: sensory changes from local nerve involvement

laboratory: Positive Congo red staining of skin biopsy with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Immunohistochemistry showing AL (light chain) amyloid subtype
Serum and urine protein electrophoresis to exclude systemic involvement
imaging: Skin ultrasound may show hypoechoic nodules
Radiologic imaging to exclude systemic amyloidosis if clinically indicated
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Exclusion of systemic amyloidosis by clinical and laboratory evaluation including cardiac and renal assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Amyloid deposits derived from keratinocytes (keratin amyloid)
Papular lesions with amyloid deposits in papillary dermis
Multisystem involvement including renal, cardiac, and neurological
Presence of systemic symptoms such as weight loss, fatigue
Positive serum or urine monoclonal proteins

redFlags: Rapid progression or ulceration of skin nodules
Signs of systemic amyloidosis such as nephrotic syndrome or cardiomyopathy
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or paraproteinemia
references: Kumar B, et al. Nodular cutaneous amyloidosis: clinical and histopathological features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
Orphanet: Nodular cutaneous amyloidosis. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
Sipe JD, et al. Amyloidosis. N Engl J Med. 2012.
